corpusSummary: Across 2026 records, this corpus surveys how large language models intersect social science—from methodological use as analytical collaborators and simulations to analyses of human–AI interaction, trust, and adoption, to applications in education, health, policy, and organizational ESG. It chronicles benefits (personalized learning, decision support, rapid analysis) alongside risks (bias, misinformation, safety, ethics), and foregrounds governance, equity-first auditing, and critical appraisal of AI’s social implications.

themes.name: LLMs as methodological tools in social science
themes.description: Papers show LLMs as analytical collaborators for coding, framing, sentiment, content analysis, and simulations, with emphasis on validation and transparent governance.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and embodiment
themes.description: Research maps trust, perceived humanness, device embodiment, social influence, and adoption barriers across health, education, work, and crisis contexts.

themes.name: AI in education, health, and well-being: benefits and risks
themes.description: GenAI enhances personalized learning, tutoring, and health information but raises concerns about safety, reliability, ethics, and dependence.

themes.name: Equity, governance, and societal implications of AI
themes.description: Work assesses fairness, bias, cultural adequacy, misinformation, governance frameworks, and policy implications across domains.
